I can’t change folder permissions from here (no tools/permissions available). I also recommend caution: the folder contains budgets and salary planning (sensitive data). Making it visible to all employees can create privacy, legal, and security risk. Before changing access, get approvals and consider safer alternatives.

If you want, I can draft an approval request or prepare redacted/public summaries — tell me which.

If you already have authorization and just need instructions, follow the appropriate steps below for common storage systems and a safe rollout checklist.

If you do not yet have approvals
- Required approvers to consult: Finance lead/CFO, HR, Legal, and InfoSec.
- Consider alternatives: publish a high-level summary (no salaries), create a redacted copy, share only specific documents, or give read-only access to a limited group rather than everyone.

Safe-rollout checklist
- Confirm no personally identifiable salary data will be exposed.
- Classify documents and mark sensitive files.
- Prepare a redacted/public folder if full exposure is not appropriate.
- Set access level to Viewer (read-only), not Editor.
- Enable auditing/logging and keep a backup snapshot.
- Notify affected stakeholders and employees of change and retention timeline.
- Consider time-limited access or staged rollout.

How to change permissions (examples)

Google Drive (Drive for Google Workspace)
1. Locate the Finance/Forecasts folder in Drive.
2. Right-click → Share.
3. Under “General access” change from “Restricted” to “Anyone in your organization” (or “Your-domain name” / “All employees”) and set role to Viewer.
4. Under “Share with people and groups” ensure no editors are added who can re-share; click Settings (gear) and disable “Editors can change permissions and share” if appropriate.
5. Click Done. Verify with InfoSec and test with a non-finance account.

Microsoft SharePoint / OneDrive (Office 365)
1. Go to the SharePoint site or OneDrive library containing the folder.
2. Select the folder → Click Share.
3. Click the link settings and choose “People in <Your Organization> with the link” (or add the built-in “Everyone except external users” group).
4. Set permission to “View” (not Edit).
5. Apply and send/share. Optionally set link expiration.
6. Update site/folder permissions in the Site Permissions admin if needed and verify.

Box
1. In Box, navigate to the folder → More Options → Settings or Share.
2. Enable a shared link for “People in [Company Name]” and set permission to Viewer.
3. Alternatively, add the company-level user group (All Company) as a collaborator with Viewer role.
4. Save and verify.

Sample approval request email to IT / Admin
Subject: Request to change access for Finance/Forecasts folder to all employees — Approval attached

Body:
Hello [IT/Access Admin name],

Please change the sharing settings for folder “Finance/Forecasts” (path: [insert path or link]) from Finance-team-only to company-wide view access (Viewer for all employees).

Reason: [brief justification]
Approvals: [CFO name], [HR lead name], [InfoSec contact name] (attached or cc’d)
Requested access level: Viewer (read-only) for all employees in domain; no external sharing.
Planned effective date: [date]
Audit/controls requested: enable audit logging, disable editors’ ability to change sharing, and create a backup snapshot before change.

Please confirm any additional steps or constraints and advise estimated time to complete.

Thank you,
[Your name, title, contact]

Next steps I can help with
- Draft a specific approval email tailored to your org and approvers.
- Create a redacted/public-summary folder and wording for employees.
- Produce a checklist for InfoSec and HR to sign off.

Which system is the folder stored in (Google Drive, SharePoint, Box, something else)? Do you already have approvals from Finance/HR/Legal/InfoSec?
